sections.h:
ANNEXES FOR THE CELEBRATIONS

Annex 1 — Celebration 3

“…Towards morning I see in the distance most beautiful trees, and oh! with what pleasure I walked on to reach them! When I was near these trees, another man of a harsh and eccentric manner asked me where I was going, and I, still walking, answered him that on that road my dear Crucified One had placed me, that I could not stop, but must follow it to the end. And I let him hear that in the end I hoped to find him.

He leaves me and I enter a magnificent wood; but to run the road that I saw marked out there were many thorn-bushes. I looked at the beautiful plants with wonderful fruit, and oh! how gladly I would have tasted one! My Crucified One picked a lovely fruit and gave it to me to eat; more than the exquisiteness of the taste of the fruit was that of having found my Good.” (Mother Rosa, from Trials and Consolations, p. 65)

Annex 2 — Celebration 4

“…I felt a sweet hand on my head and, leaning on it, a sweet refreshment calmed me, dispelling all fear, and I remained in sweet tranquillity.

But, since the intellect always wants to reason and to have knowledge of things that are mysterious, so, reasoning, I went on to enquire how it was and whose it was, that sweet hand which had left my soul so well. Convinced that I needed nothing, I had the finest and greatest knowledge of everything. Oh! the goodness of my dear Crucified One, who always in his infinite charity and mercy deigns to instruct this servant of his who never manages to understand; but I realise that I am beside myself.” (from Trials and Consolations, p. 62)

Annex 3 — Celebration 5

“…Tired, I sat down and meanwhile I prayed, when a group of little girls came skipping up to me and, seeing me, drew near. I asked them whether they knew who had created them; they looked at me as if I had said something more than new.

— Do you not know that it was God? — (I said to one of them).

— Who is this you tell me of?

Poor creatures! Moved to compassion I tried to make them know my God, and how they should thank him because he had put them into the world. Oh! how I hungered, and how I would have wished that they had understood everything in a flash! After I had been instructing them for a long while, some dishevelled young women arrive and sharply rebuke me, taking their little girls by the hand. I begged them to leave them with me. Oh! how many things they said to me! They loaded me with insults and went away; but I thought to myself of a means of getting them back. Oh! how they moved me to compassion! I managed to get some of them, but not those I wanted.

Oh! how immense, my God, is your charity! Creatures so fierce, and yet you bear with them! Every minute you give me new lessons in patience, charity and humility…” (from Trials and Consolations, p. 207)

Annex 4 — Celebration 6

“…Quite exhausted in strength I fell asleep sitting on the ground, my head resting on a stone. I found myself immersed in the sweetest conversations, and it seemed to me that I had with me my Lord who, taking me by the hand, showed me delightful works of creation: a vast field, whose end could not be seen. He said to me:

— Look! this Work of mine will be without end.

He made me turn, and on the right there was a large and high mountain:

— All of this must be levelled! There is no remedy, because it was built by barbarous people, and I let it be done, because you yourself must remove all these big stones. There will be some that will make you sweat blood: this will serve so that it need not grow again, but the field will become beautiful and many lilies will spring up in it. My Father will take great pleasure in it.

I listened to him with a love that made me blissful. At last we arrived at the bottom of a cave, which was as dark as could be:

— Do you see this darkness? Well, you must give it light. The inhabitants all live in the dark…” (from Trials and Consolations, p. 423)

Annex 5 — Celebration 10

Sweet Love! I have served you ill, mistaking the path!

“…Thus resigned, I ran on; but a deep sadness held me bound: all my mental faculties tied up, I was like a senseless woman who walks, not knowing where and not even realising she is tired, a true donkey that goes and goes as long as its legs hold it up and then throws itself on the ground. So it happened to this slave of yours. Shaken by weariness, I noticed that I was in a wood thick with trees: a sepulchral silence! My God, where am I? Who brought me here? My voice:

— Your carelessness!

How is it that, without noticing, I find myself in so terrible a labyrinth? My God, have pity! Ah! my Master, my Lord, mercy on my fault! And I kept saying to myself: so I have been careless! Alas, what have I done? I threw myself on the ground among those plants: My Lord! I deserve nothing but to be devoured by wild beasts. I understand it: I deserve neither mercy nor pardon; let the vipers of this frightful wood devour me and I, resigned, will suffer the penalty. Oh! I offended you, sweet love! Yes, I have served you ill, mistaking the path, and here I am! I took hold of some thorny branches and with all my strength beat this donkey, because through its fault I had committed such carelessness; and I wept bitterly. A light suddenly (appears to me) and I feel myself seized by the arm and told:

— Enough!

Oh! my angel! Prostrate, with hands joined, which were bloodied, I told him weeping that I had committed that carelessness and that surely my Lord was displeased at it and that I deserved nothing but to be devoured by the beasts.

He looked at me and, smiling, lifted me up.

— Ah! why, my dear guide, have you allowed me to stray from the path? He answered me nothing. He looked at my hands and at the ground where the blood was, and then said to me:

— This had to be shed for the good of the fields that you will have to set in order…” (from Trials and Consolations, pp. 485–486)

Annex 6 — Celebration 12

“… Ah! my Good, you alone could say it! Oh! you who are my Paradise! How can I make you known to all the world. Oh! how many there are who do not know you, and those who have known you flee from you so as never to have seen you; I would like to run everywhere and cry out loud that all should come and love you…”

“… Oh! what thirst! my Good, you quenched the thirst of a Samaritan woman, ah, let pity move you at my burning thirst. Oh! love, let the fire of your Love be my only nourishment, and when I go to sinners to convert them let my words have such efficacy as to convert the whole world; I suffer too much at seeing you offended! Oh! what a thirst, my Good, I have to give my life for them, and so be able, like the martyrs, to be put on the pyre for you. Oh! endless ardour! why shall I never succeed in quenching my thirst?…”

(Mother Rosa, Memoirs, 1.1, pp. 30 and 38)

Annex 7 — Celebration 15

“… ah! courage, to fight well against the wretched powers of sense and flesh and to will at all costs that our spirit be always victorious in us, and to seek to respond to every inspiration that our Jesus never ceases to give us and so many times makes us feel strongly, and we, with the utmost indifference, reject them, as if they were things of no account; and yet one day a great account will be asked of us for these. Woe to that creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in his mercy, gives her!…”

(Mother Rosa, Letters, vol. 1, p. 201)

“… for charity’s sake let us be humble, or Jesus will humble us. Yes, this I can assure you: one act of vainglory, and at once God with his dear hand humbles us to the abyss of our nothingness; one act of humility, and the dear Eternal Father comforts us, making his work shine forth.

“I urge you to practise this virtue and I beg you for the love of God and for the love you say you bear me, because without it I shall not be able to see you run in the way of perfection. Without humility one cannot enter Paradise. Console me by giving me proofs that you will always practise it and that from now on it will be your chief thought to come to have it well rooted in your heart.

Listen, for now I cannot dwell any longer on this matter, for I should never finish. The affection I have for this virtue is too great…”.

(Mother Rosa, Letters, vol. 2, p. 315)

Annex 8 — Celebration 16

“… No, let not slanders, worries, anguish make you fall short of the sublime grace you received from God.

I too was slandered, despised, ill-treated: and not the slightest thought against the holy vocation ever came to me.

Be strong against all assaults; fight valiantly and you will come out victorious. Always keep in mind the words I say to you at this moment, put them into practice and you will find yourselves content.

Do not do as those who excuse themselves because of slanders, and leave off serving the Lord. Who is better than the Lord? Is it not better to serve the Creator?

Look at the Crucified One when tribulations assail you: and who suffered more than he? This Lamb, God, without stain, suffered for us, receiving insults, slaps, blows and the most infamous slanders! Who, then, was more slandered than he for love of you, who suffered on a cross the most infamous death, the most painful?

He will be our fortress, our guide; he will fight with us and will be our courage…”

(from Mother Rosa’s talk to the Sisters of Piacenza, 30 August 1898)

Annex 9 — Celebration 17

“…after a few days I went to the Archbishop and told him what Frassinetti had said to me and (without telling him how it had gone) I gave him the corrections that I had made above in the booklet, and he told me with surprise that they were exactly those he had wished to be removed… Those that I had put back began to disturb me, because an inner voice kept tormenting me, saying that I must show them to him, that it was his work, but I drove it away and, to put it better, did not understand what was wanted; one evening I said: what do you want, my dear Crucified One? Why must I show this writing, what is it to serve for? He answered me: for the work I want; it will be great! My God! I began to think and understood nothing: where is it to be, who is to do this work? I felt so confused I stopped thinking about it and began to pray, clasped to my dear Crucified One, and a voice that was certainly his – my Good’s – said to me: I want this work from you. Take to the Archbishop the writing you have. Oh! how my mind was thrown into confusion: another work, how could I undertake it? What shame to say this to the Archbishop! Oh! my God, I feel that my strength does not reach to doing what you command me, I feel I am dying at the mere thought of it, and my children, the mother, and I wept, no, my Jesus, I have not the courage, I cannot! and for several days I went on weeping but never made up my mind. At last I revealed it to the Confessor under seal… and I could not do this, leave them, no, my children, besides, the mere thought of having to leave them was an agony and I kept saying to myself (no, it will never be – no) and the Good Shepherd allowed me to go to Rome, he provided me with letters of recommendation; it seemed to me that I had already won the victory; never (I kept telling myself) will Pope Pius IX allow a mother to leave her children, and a mother to whom I was so greatly attached, and also my poor old father, who both loved me so much and, one might say, in their last years adored me. Ah! no, my Love! you will not allow it, your Vicar will give me peace and relief in so cruel a battle, his word will be a balm for me on the wound of sorrow bitterly opened. I expressed this desire of mine…”

“we went as far as Rome, arriving at one o’clock on 1 January 1866… – We asked for an audience, which we had on 3 January at five o’clock in the afternoon: it was a private audience. Oh! this day I shall never forget, my hopes vanished and a most bitter knife came to wound me deeply. I had already had the Rules given to the Supreme Pontiff, I mean those that my Dear Crucified One had dictated to me, which, according to the Holy Father’s words, were like the commandments. As soon as I was at his Holy Feet – Pius IX’s – he blessed me and, raising me with his hand, which held mine tight, told me that he had read those rules and that they were truly beautiful and that I must not delay putting them into effect. Oh! I threw myself on the ground and, weeping, said to him: Holiness, I have two children, a Father and a mother, both of them old, my children are small; he answered me: it does not matter – God wills it so. Ah! no, Holiness, God according to the Holy Gospel will ask me for an account of my children, and I wept bitterly, I love them too much, I cannot leave them – Holiness, it is impossible; the Holy Father stopped and in a severe tone said to me: well then, if you do not do what God wants of you you will have remorse, for all the time of your life your conscience will reproach you, and you will no longer have peace. I was frightened and no, Holiness, I answered him, I want to do God’s will. He resumed: good, and in the manner of one inspired he said to me: this Institute will spread rapidly like the flight of the dove into all parts of the world. God will take care of your children – you take care of God in his work. What a prophecy! Dear Holy Father Pius IX, I stood up and could hardly utter words. I felt my chest breaking, he drew me to his writing desk and gave me two photographs of himself, writing a motto on each. Oh! how I felt! nothing was a comfort to me. He went on: Papa and Mama will resign themselves.

You will lack nothing, everything will be given to you! (from the File on the Foundation of the Institute)

Annex 10 — Celebration 19

Let us think that in these days we have the model of the holy humility practised by Jesus, and the Church keeps us occupied in these days teaching us the way to imitate this model of every virtue, beginning with the going to the Jordan. What a lowering! the most perfect, the purest God-Man wished to submit to being on a level with the sinner, purified with the water of holy baptism in the Jordan, but heaven opened, and a voice that could not contain itself cried out: this is my Son!

Jesus, what are you doing? Enough! But no, he goes on to submit his delicate humanity to still greater torments…

Pray and love one another with one and the same love and take care to reach that beautiful unity of thinking and acting [so that] all together you may form one heart, one mind, because you are all tending to one centre, which is God. And so true charity and love towards you must be so sincere that one’s own good must also be towards one’s sister. If you become so, the Spirit of God will reign in you for eternity…”

(Letters, Volume 1, p. 377)

Annex 11 — Celebration 20

… My angel seized me by the arm and, shaking me from so horrible a lethargy, gave me strength and, pointing out to me a long and painful road that awaited me, said to me:

— Go! God sends you there: you will have much to suffer, but you will be sustained by the strength of the Lord.

I looked at him and, weeping, said to him:

— Ah! promise me that you will always be with me. And he:

— Am I not always near you?

— No! — I said to him. And he, still smiling at me:

— I shall be with you, do not be afraid! The dragon will not move under my foot. You will have to struggle with all sorts of people; they will want to stop you on the way, and even those who are with you will urge you to turn back. Woe to you if you listen to the human claws that will be raised up to frighten you.

I look at the road and feel myself invaded by a horrible fear; as in a flash my whole being is terrified. My angel notices this disturbance of mine and in a severe tone says to me:

— Think of fulfilling the will of God: woe to you if you turn back!

And he vanished. Mute, my forehead resting on my hand, I stood motionless. After a long while I resumed:

— Where is the strength, my Crucified One, to do what you command me? This poor slave of yours is always ready for sacrifice under the yoke of work: she will never dare stop! (Your orders) will be carried out!…”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 520–521)

Annex 12 — Celebration 22

“…Heaven rejoices at the good that is done in the vineyard of the Lord and the angels themselves go about gathering the ripe fruits and carry them before the throne of God the Father. And sweet Jesus, with a gaze full of satisfaction, admires the fruit of his most precious blood. He, lovable, infinite in his love, bought us so great a treasure that with it he could raise our poor soul to the seats of eternal life, which are acquired only by toil and suffering. Love… love…”

(from Rosa Gattorno, a Mother, pp. 132–133)

Annex 13 — Celebration 23

“…Look! this Work of mine will be without end.

He made me turn, and on the right there was a large and high mountain:

— All of this must be levelled! There is no remedy, because it was built by barbarous people, and I let it be done, because you yourself must remove all these big stones. There will be some that will make you sweat blood: this will serve so that it need not grow again, but the field will become beautiful and many lilies will spring up in it. My Father will take great pleasure in it.

I listened to him with a love that made me blissful. At last we arrived at the bottom of a cave, which was as dark as could be:

— Do you see this darkness? Well, you must give it light. The inhabitants all live in the dark”

— Oh! my Master! do not leave me here, for pity’s sake! — and I trembled.

— Not now, but unfortunately you will enter it and you will have to give light to those who live in darkness.

What I felt was such that I hardly gave any thought to what was to happen to me. At last a great brightness opens: there were great things that I can no longer describe, and he says to me:

— Only charity and humility enter this dwelling. And he vanished.

I woke up and looked all around me: where am I, my Love? But was I awake or sleeping? Ah, what a simpleton! Of course: a dream produced by weariness! I fell asleep with the desire to have my Good, and I dreamt of him. But the mountain? And I went on repeating to myself all that I had dreamt.

And I fell asleep again. And here once more is my Saviour and Master and Beloved!

— It is time to go where you think you have dreamt. But it is not a dream, it is reality! Take care to suffer with relish and resignation. This is my will!

I started up and, prostrate on the ground, thanked my Lord for it.

— Here I am, ready at your slightest sign!”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 423–424)

Annex 14 — Celebration 26

… — Do not doubt, for my Master is that God who feeds the birds, and who can fear not having what is needed? (cf. Mt 6:26).

I look around and see nothing. The field was without trees, not even a farmhouse was in sight. My God! what will become of this poor creature if she is not provided with what is necessary? Teach me what I must do.

— Trust, and nothing else — says my voice to me.

Now it grows dark. She no longer spoke, but from her face one could see that she was saying a great deal. A most fierce struggle arose in me, but I held firmly to the word: Only trust!

At last I hear a noise and anxiously look: it was a peasant with a cart and two oxen, which he was urging on to make them go. As soon as he sees us he gives a loud: Oh!

— Come!

But I was afraid; she looked at me as if she wanted to say to me: you see where you have brought me? what will become of us! The cart draws near and the good man invites us to climb up, telling us that he had orders from his master to come and fetch us to take us to his farmhouse, which was awaiting us with a good supper prepared. I turned to that frightened one and begged her to follow me by climbing into the cart. Not very willingly she climbed up and the good man led us along the road from which, after a short climb, a large farmhouse could be seen.

— There — the good man began to say — is where we must go. See how beautiful our farm is!

She looked at me with two big eyes as if she wanted to reproach me for having climbed into the cart; seeing her so, I said to her:

— Why so much fear? Oh! how small a heart you have, filled only with mistrust! Oh! you are too human. The fields are God’s, what is being cultivated in them is for him: how can you doubt that he himself is thinking of us? Oh! I am happy! I feel it: the cart that is carrying me is his, the man will be according to his desire; wherever he takes us we shall surely find our Master…”.

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 398–399)

Annex 15 — Celebration 27

“… So I set out, and the sufferings and pains I felt from it were sweet to me. And, as if I had been close to my Saviour, I reasoned about it. I felt many things that were more than those that came from me. I never reached the top: the more road I made, the more it seemed to me that the mountain rose. Ah! my chest ached, my knees buckled and my strength no longer held. Oh! how like my Saviour!

The night was dark; the track was hardly marked on this mountain; I could not even find where to rest this treasure of mine, to which I felt so bound in affection and which I adored with the greatest veneration. What to do? When I looked at the depth of this mountain I was frightened: one single instant of a false move, and I could plunge into that abyss! I began to tremble, when the thought is suggested to me that I had with me the treasure of my Crucified One. All fear vanished in me.

Meanwhile I kept trying more and more to climb, in the hope of finding a small corner where I could stop, and I was thinking this:

— Oh! fortunate apostles who, before Calvary, saw and enjoyed the delights of Tabor, and saw my God beautiful in all his infinite majesty!

At last I found a small stretch of ground and thought of stopping to take strength and spend the night there. I had one trouble: that I did not know how to lay the cross. What did I do? I spread out my habit and then laid it on it with all delicacy.

Oh! how beautiful you are! you served as the last bed for my God who expired upon you! But how shall I ever be able to carry you on my breast as you deserve? My voice:

— Take your rest upon it: you will gain strength for walking.

I did not hesitate a moment and lay down on the cross. Oh! gentle and sweet rest! what contentment I felt! I fell asleep, if sleep it can be called, because I learned the most beautiful lessons of mystical theology; I held a conversation and had the most beautiful answers even on cases of conscience. How well he explained to me his law and that of the Church, the parables of the holy Gospel!

At last, waking late in the morning:

— What? am I alone? Where is the one with whom I was conversing until now?

I looked around: I am truly alone! Strengthened and as if I had come from a lavish meal, I got up and knelt to make a little adoration of the holy Wood. But all that I had heard was always before my mind. My voice:

— Take up your cross and walk!

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 194–195)

Annex 16 — Celebration 29

“… — It is God’s will that this poor slave, alone on the thorny path (should find herself) on the journey, so that his most holy will may be perfectly fulfilled.

— Is it not enough? You must not teach anyone to walk in this way, because no one entered upon this. It is God’s will that everyone should have his own guide.

Having said this, he vanished. How to understand this mystery? For me alone! Unhappy woman! how my wickednesses have reduced me! And I began to weep. An old shepherd came up to me and asked me the cause of my weeping. Nothing! And I ran on, and he, though old, kept following me. I turned and begged him to go away, that I needed nothing, only what he could not give me.

— You are mistaken — he said to me. I stopped:

— Do you know whom I seek?

— Of course: it is God! — How do you know?

— Because I come from him. — Oh! tell me!

— He has placed in you a new delight; everything is greatly ordered. Your anguish is moved by love and, so as not to let you die of languor, burnt by the flames of his fiery love, he keeps this communication suspended.

I felt beside myself! — For a long time yet? — This is kept for him alone. — Tell me: who are you? — My bride will tell you — and he vanished.

Saint Joseph! he was very beautiful! And I sat down (thinking): “The Mother of God will tell me!” So I shall see her, I shall speak to her! Oh! when? And I sighed:

— How painful is the journey of this life! A voice answers me:

— And just as meritorious! Rise, and do not lose time! Go to the top of that mountain, where there are some shepherd girls who do not care for their sheep, and so several have been lost, others are about to fall over the edge…”.

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 162–163)

Annex 17 — Celebration 30

“… My Crucified One! when, face down on the ground, having no more strength from the oppression of sorrow, I was choking, he raised me up and nourished me with his love. If my bones bent, my Crucified One filled me with the nectar of his love.

So, walking among crags and woods, always on the path marked by his footsteps, I did not notice that, all pricked, I was in pain; I felt a giant’s strength when I found myself face to face with people who said all sorts of rude things to me.

My Crucified One! he showed himself beautiful to me and took great delight in what I was suffering; then my love grew towards my persecutors and, if it had not been that they were offending God, I would have wished that they had been doubled. I found that they were leading me from Pilate and the judges; I was ashamed, but in my mind I meditated on the steps of my Saviour…”..

(from Trials and Consolations, p. 52)

Annex 18 — Celebration 31

Penances for a soul in purgatory whose debt can be paid only with blood

“… I fell asleep in that bush where I found myself sitting, so exhausted in strength. Was I dreaming or was I awake? I saw a soul that was in purgatory and with joined hands it begged me to tell a person who was suffering greatly, because she had not given what was in a piece of furniture in her house. A voice, whose owner I could not see, told me to pray for this soul and that she needed to satisfy a debt, but it could be cancelled only with blood. I started and looked around. Oh! — I said to myself — it was a dream: the exhaustion, the unhappy position I was in, caused such sleep. I tried to get up to set out, but it was still dark night, all silence, nothing could be seen: I could hardly see my path. I had cold and hunger so that I could not stand… So, pensive over the decision to take, I sat down and thought that, as soon as it was light, I would find herbs or wild fruits and would feed myself.

My reasoning not yet finished, the sound of a bell is heard. Oh! here nearby is my God! Without further thought, I run to where the sound (was heard coming from). In the middle of a pleasant wood there was a little chapel; I entered and threw myself at the feet of my God, beating my breast: I am not worthy, my Love, to receive you, but my breast pants to possess you, my heart throbs to have you within it.

Now the candles are lit: in a moment I shall possess you! So it happened. Oh! bread of heaven, what strength you give to one who is weak! My Love! Having said this, I remained absorbed in him. A voice said to me:

— I, for you, so much charity, and you, for those two souls who suffer so much, have you no charity?

— Oh! how, my Love? So it was not a dream, but reality, what happened to me in that bush. I shall do all that they have asked of me.

After a long while, recovering myself, I took to my path to set out to perform the charity, for which blood was needed, for the one and the other. So, pensive and hurrying to arrive, entering the farmhouse, I set about doing what I had promised, offering my blood to my God to ransom that soul in purgatory together with the other.

And ever full of strength I went back to continue on my path; and I always remembered the grace I had received that morning; it so occupied me that I thanked my God warmly for it.”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 309–311)

Annex 19 — Celebration 35

“…And that field? Nothing had been sown in it; all the trees without fruit, many were about to wither. The ground was full only of weeds. I wept greatly over it and prayed much that God would water with his grace the roots of those trees and make them fruitful; that he should pay no heed to the ingratitude of those workers, but only to his infinite mercy and to the good of his field; that if he did not make those plants flourish, I was not able to make them bear fruit. I prayed and, at the end, fell asleep weeping.

Starting up, I saw a beautiful picture of the Most Holy Virgin: in her hand she had a most beautiful basket of exquisite fruits. Oh! how my soul was filled with joy! O my Mother! are these the fruits of this field? will they be the same in the future, oh! and pleasing to your Son? will they be like these that you have?

— Yes — and I remained in ecstasy from the consolation.

In that position I asked her to give me one. She did not answer me. I insisted still more; she took one and said to me: — In this you will find all the tastes of those for whom you have made sacrifice for me. How I savoured it! Oh! lovable Mother! for so little, you give me so much! What do I feel I want to sacrifice for love of you! What ardour was born in me! I would have wished to find something to offer and sacrifice: I have nothing more! Everything, everything I have consecrated to you.”

… Oh! my Love! how I too would like to know how to praise you and make you praised, love you and make you loved! But how? I am so wretched that I have nothing to offer you. I had a miserable will and this, as soon as I knew it, I at once gave to you: nothing is left to me but this miserable humanity to drag wherever you command me to go. No longer mine, I drag it only where it pleases you and it will always be, with your help, an instrument of your divine will.”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 192; 308)

Annex 20 — Celebration 36

… Absorbed in deep meditation on the Passion of my Lord, I passed in a flight to God’s mercy towards man. I found myself plunged in an abyss and felt wholly pressed down, as if in that abyss every fault were to be dispersed: I rejoiced at it! When suddenly the view changed into God’s justice. How to describe this? The smallest imperfections are written out and pictured before one. The God of mercies is a most severe judge! I trembled from head to foot; a strong inner agitation made me unable to recover myself in mercy. No! wretched me! Forgetful of anything created and of myself, I thought of one thing alone and this occupied all my mental faculties: my Love the Judge! I felt myself shuddering all over and wept violently. My voice:

— Why do you let yourself be carried away so meanly?

Full of shame I asked God’s pardon for it and always thought how mercy, for one who loves, surpasses justice (cf. Jas 2:13).”

(from Trials and Consolations, p. 372)

Annex 21 — Celebration 37

“… One can never come to believe that in this land of work there can be creatures so ungrateful for the good received; and yet, in the vast field of the Lord, unfortunately there are. My voice, while I was reasoning:

— And how many I had when I preached to my ungrateful people!

I stopped to think and ponder well these holy words and, after a long while, I answered:

— Oh! how I must always complain!

I almost felt in me a sort of displeasure because I could not succeed in getting everyone to respond to the great benefits of the Lord.

I began to say:

— My God, how must I conduct myself?

My voice:

— Always do as much good as possible to your neighbour, without caring whether they will respond or not. Never judge and accuse your brother of ingratitude: always seek to excuse all the actions of others. Take with you a good worker and bring me to that field, where there is need to straighten some plant that is bending badly.”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 341–342)

Annex 22 — Celebration 38

“…Truly, my daughters, all that you see of greatness in the Institute, do not think that it is I, no: you owe it to the Holy Mother. I am nothing but a most unworthy creature. Another creature far more worthy, one who would have worked better than I, ought to have been chosen for the spread of this Institute, to direct you, who are all angels, all beautiful souls.

I am the vilest creature, the most wretched: but good God and the Holy Mother turned their merciful gaze upon me and worked great things in me. I work, I toil; but it is all divine power that dwells in me, although unworthy, drained of strength, I give myself wholly for you and never shall I fail my vocation.

Daughters, one promise I want from you on this day: that you be faithful to the Institute and to Holy Mother Church. No, daughters, let not slanders, worries, anguish make you fall short of the holy vocation, of the sublime grace you received from God.

I too was slandered, despised, ill-treated: and not the slightest thought against the holy vocation ever came to me.

Be strong against all assaults; fight valiantly and you will come out victorious. Always keep in mind the words I say to you at this moment, put them into practice and you will find yourselves content.

I love you all in God, I hold you to my breast and I devote myself in everything to your service. I cannot say more: my thought is God alone, my only support, and no one will be able to turn me away from him. I love you, but in God, in that immense love which remains in all hearts: be grateful. Pray for me and I shall keep you engraved in my heart. May God bless you!”

(excerpts from Mother Rosa’s Talk to the Sisters of Piacenza, 30 August 1898)

Annex 23 — Celebration 39

“…Meanwhile my thought (was): what will become of those creatures who went away? What a sight! A picture is presented to me of the future of a creature who does not respond to the graces of the Lord and with disdain turns her back on him, throwing the precious gift to the ground. That soul was so strange, so penanced, that it tore me apart to see her. An iron bit crossed her forehead as if crushing a rebellious part. I understood well all its meaning, because it was her own will: the proudest power that lords it over all the others, because pride (is) self-love that will not remain subject to any obedience and judges in the way that pleases it most.

Horrible pain! An iron bit that held her forehead tight and she was bound to a block (in such a way) that she could not move in the least! Finally, she languished with thirst; crystal-clear water was before her, but she was forbidden to drink of it, because she had made herself unworthy of it. Every part of her body was tormented by certain ugly creatures who were around her and gave her immense annoyance. Oh! what a sight! I looked at her a little and then, unable to bear it, I tried to turn my gaze elsewhere.

— Oh! my Good! If these pains could be seen before leaving this earth, they would be converted.

My voice:

— They feel them, they feel them even in life, but they do not see them!

— Surely, if such a picture were seen, no creature would dare fail the promises made.

My voice:

— If at every step this were painted before them, their tenacity would overcome every terror. What did Judas not do?

Oh! what did I not feel!”

Along the way I thought that so many souls will remain a prey, because they lack light. A voice lets me know that God does not fail to communicate it to them; but it is they who do not want to listen; and at the bottom of their heart there reigns a seed of fleshly affection and this lords it over them with principal dominion.”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 94–96)

Annex 24 — Celebration 43

“…suddenly a rapture so strong and I found myself in spirit in a church where my Good had been exposed during the day.

I saw the church all illuminated, resplendent with light, an infinity of Angels adoring their God, my Beloved!

I saw all the doors closed and found myself alone; I approached the Tabernacle and a crowd of Angels was there, a light so vivid dazzled me. I saw my Beloved of immense beauty, a fire burned in me…” (Mem. 1, p. 66).

“…ravished in him I saw the church all splendour, the good souls who had received him and many angels who stood near… in an attitude of adoration… more was the light… that surrounded the ciborium and in this light I saw the Sovereign of Heaven…” (Mem. 1.1, pp. 152–153).

“…yesterday, the day of the Body of the Lord, I was… in adoration, while… I was absorbed in God and… my Jesus who said to me: look, and it seemed to me that I saw all the souls of Paradise, these are those who received me in life… they were of a most resplendent light…”. (Mem. 3, p. 41)

“…so, my daughter, this is all my work and it was the first thing I put into your heart, the repugnance to all that will be a worldly satisfaction…”. (Mem. 1, p. 130)

(excerpts from the Memoirs of M. Rosa)

Annex 25 — Celebration 44

“… Yes, my God is all love for his creatures.

I realised that she was wholly ignorant in this matter and begged her to listen to me. Meanwhile all the others gathered around me and I instructed them on all the points of our holy Religion, going on to make them know the differences between the love of God and that of creatures; that the heart of the creature has need of love, and how, not knowing the sublimity of the love of God, they love creatures. In the love of God there is the whole divine essence and it has no limits or end; that of creatures is deceptive and soon vanishes, withers like the rose cut from the plant and placed in the sun: the disillusion with the transient things of earth is plainly seen; but the love of my God, Master and Lord, burns ever more brightly in the heart of the creature and finally, with its rays, ravishes and consumes it in its most sweet divine ether. Oh, yes, Love!”

(from Trials and Consolations, p. 365)

Annex 26 — Celebration 49

“… I saw myself in a most beautiful chalice and, as a Victim, my soul was being offered to the Eternal Father, surrounded by a most vivid light; I came to myself and was endowed with strength to face all sacrifices.” (Mem. 1.1, pp. 97–98).

“…I placed myself in that chalice, telling the Eternal Father to be so kind as to look at me, that I was covered, soaked in the Blood of my love Jesus. On the Altar of Sacrifice there are two victims, look upon us! And so saying I remained absorbed in God, I remained so. He let me see that he had accepted that offering of sacrifice with much pleasure…” (Mem. 1.1, p. 179) (excerpts from the Memoirs of Mother Rosa)

Annex 27 — Celebration 51

“…This said, a great road opens. Transported by the ardent desire to be able to consume myself wholly in the service of my God, I quickened my pace as much as I could. At the end of this road there was a very high mountain, all stony; every now and then a bush. My track was marked on harsh and sharp stones. At the sight of so steep a climb I was frightened; but I was very glad to be able to climb it. I clambered up with all the strength I had; I tried not to slip.

When I was halfway (up the climb), I found a large cross laid out and, prostrate, I prayed before it. But I felt I could not move. What can this be? Oh! my treasure! I kissed and kissed again that wood, and saw so clearly all that my God had suffered upon it. From weariness and the pain of all my limbs I fell asleep with my head resting at the foot of the holy Wood. My voice:

— Wake up and take this cross and follow your path.

It was very large; I did not dare put it on my shoulder because I was not worthy. What did I do? I held it close and embraced it (saying):

— On my breast you shall lie and I shall climb Calvary!…”

(from Trials and Consolations, p. 193)

Annex 28 — Celebration 52

“…Take a look at where you are, where God has placed you. Look at the vast field and delightful garden of the gardener Redeemer, look to what sublimity of greatness he has raised you, to be an active part of a new Order of his that is being born in the womb of his beloved Bride. One day we shall know in all its extent the worth, the power, the eternal glory for whoever has had a part in it. All this we shall see in the glory of the blessed, where, by pure mercy, we must hope to go. Up there things are seen so clearly and the false reasoning of down here is ended.”

(Vol. 1, Letters, p. 304)

Annex 29 — Celebration 53

“…I also urge you to care for the sick, to go to them with love, with reverence, as if going to Jesus; if sleep comes upon me I shall try to get up and do all I can to wake myself, I must picture myself before Jesus, who counts all that I do for this sick person. See, I went there for 25 years and it seemed to me I was going to Paradise; see, there is no consolation on earth like this, I have not felt it any more since I no longer go. Yes, do everything in the spirit. I am in this hospital, this woman full of insects, I dress her sores, I relieve her, ah! what delight to think of relieving a creature of Jesus; yes, there is no duty that brings such consolation as this; to return home in the morning and say: I have dressed the wound of my Jesus…”

(Talk of M. Rosa to the Sisters of Ferrara)

Annex 30 — Celebration 54

Oh! it is you whom we have been awaiting for so long! May you be blessed by God!

— Tell me, who are you?

— A worker who awaits you so that you may give me work. But how many there are there like me!

— Have they all already begun to work?

— None. I tell you that all are awaiting you.

— How did you know that I was to come?

— For many years we have longed to be able to serve the Lord by working in his vineyard, but it was never granted us. We shed many prayers and tears, but nothing! We saw the field beautiful and ever flourishing, but greatly in need of being cultivated. Beautiful plants! and many are spoiled at the root. At last, after so much sighing, there came a handsome and gracious shepherd, at the mere sight of whom we were left in ecstasy and, in a supernatural manner, he announced your coming to us and promised great things to whoever will be faithful to you in the work. And he vanished.

— Ah! — I cried out — It was my Lord! Tell me where he stopped to speak to you and the ground on which he set his most holy foot.

Oh! how breathlessly I ran to see where my God had been!”

“… I threw myself on the ground and with all my soul kissed and kissed again that ground. And then I would have wished to enclose it in my breast, which was throbbing violently. The poor woman, who still did not understand and whose heart had not yet tasted and experienced the effects of God’s love, looked at me, and then (remained) unmoved, bored, and moreover had little regard for it. I gave thought to nothing, but that ground… Here, my Love, you have been! Oh! how strong is this thought!”

“… On arriving I found indeed a beautiful and immense, pleasant field. The workers all around made a great fuss of me.

— Tell me, have you all seen my Lord? and heard him spoken of? Oh! how beautiful he is!

Not all (they answered). They invited me to sit down and bustled about to make me notice the beauty of the field. There were fruit trees of every kind and of many of these they made me observe that a little woodworm had crept in around them, which gnawed their pith and they were dying. Other weeds, which stretched long around the vine and took away its sap, so that it could not (bear fruit). Among nearly all the wheat darnel had sprung up. From the sight and together with the account a serious thought seized me: so vast a field, with so great a variety of crops, and so few workers! I leaned back, pensive; but my voice:

— Who will do this? You and the workers, or the Master?

I was ashamed and, smiling, told those dear creatures to set to work. Several of them tell me that they lack tools and that, if I do not provide for them, they cannot obey me.

— Without faith! Come with me!”.

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 136–138)

Annex 31 — Celebration 55

“… my Saviour appeared to me suddenly all clothed in a most beautiful mantle radiant with Light; he held a golden Chalice in his hand, it was empty; once more he tilts it towards me as if to show me that it was empty and vanished. I could say nothing, I remained thus with my mind in him and thought of him alone. My Love, how much goodness towards one who is laden with demerits! The next day, my meditation scarcely begun, behold I am absorbed in my Good and had nothing more than Love; my soul was blissful, my intellect was furnished with the most beautiful knowledge and lights…”

(from the Memoirs, 1.1, p. 180)

ANNEXES FOR THE RETREATS

Annex 32 — Retreat 1

“… my Good! such was the union with my God that as soon as I began to pray, behold at once I was absorbed in him and always saw new things. Now Seated on a heap of clouds all radiant and then he taught me, corrected me, showed me how I should act for his Work, everything, in a word how I should conduct myself. It always seems as if I did not live but within me there were a person who acted and lived for me; continually I saw before me so beautiful a light that even when I listened to someone speaking, if I was not on guard over myself, I remained enchanted.”

“… behold near the wall on the right side where I was turned a great brightness, and a large flame of fire, in the middle it was a little darker; it was so beautiful that I was ravished and it stayed still for some minutes and then moved and came above my head. What I felt as it drew near I cannot express but it was a most sweet nectar that intoxicated me; when it was on my Head it vanished because I no longer saw the brightness it sent forth and I returned again to myself, only there remained to me such a union with God that I felt…”. (Mother Rosa, Memoirs, 1.1, p. 64 and 4.4, p. 59)

Annex 33 — Retreat 2

“…I was very distressed some days ago because I lacked the money to pay a bill that they wanted paid at once. My God! what providence, after praying much and when the prayer was finished, a few hours later a lady came and brought me everything I needed, telling me that she had been sent by a person to bring me that money and however much I did to find out who had sent her she would tell me nothing, repeating to me: this person is unknown, pray, and she left me! I was so confused and at once went to the Chapel to thank my God for the Providence he deigned to send me.” (from the Memoirs, 1.1, pp. 71–72)

Annex 34 — Retreat 3

“… we must fear nothing, because we have God with us.

And I began to speak of my Master, telling her that she worked for him; but it was clear that she did not know him. She remained enchanted.

— What? — I said to her — so much work, and yet you do not know at all the Master, the Teacher, our Lord, his riches, his treasures? Oh poor creature! And anxiously she said to me: — Tell me, for charity’s sake! I felt wholly changed. It seemed to me that I truly loved him; yes, I served him, but I did not love him and felt nothing for him; only the duty of serving him!

— Ah no! he wants to be loved, and more than work he wants love. Martha, Martha! — said our Master — you are too anxious! While Magdalene felt much love for him and gave herself wholly to love, reckoning work less (cf. Lk 10:38–42). So we must do, because work must never be excessive for prayer, because only by praying and meditating on the Passion of our divine Master do we learn to know him and love him much. Prayer obtains much, it is necessary above all when we are in dryness, even when temptation troubles us, making us weary in prayer: it is then that we must force ourselves to get through all the prayers.

The effort that must be made renders our prayer more acceptable to God than when in it we find relief, recollection and union with God. The satisfaction of feeling that consolation in prayer God permits to beginners, so that they may attach themselves to that taste and so be able to go forward, but without progressing; as do instead those who pray without taste, without consolations, whom faith alone guides and assures: these walk the way of perfection and take giant strides.

She listened to me attentively and every so often interrupted me to get clarifications. Fervent and full of that enthusiasm, what would this creature not have done! But I restrained her; only one thing I left her in her fervour, to strive to attain (so great a good) herself too. She surprised me by saying to me: — Shall I come to obtain this without thinking of anything else? — Yes — I answered her — provided you keep firmly to your fervour.

Happy, she gave herself wholly to denying herself in order to be wholly God’s. And I left her…”.

“… In what we try to do for God we always have extraordinary help.

Poor woman! She understood this language little. One could see that the Lord’s grace was at work, but she knew nothing. I tried to instruct her well and she showed herself very glad. Oh! how, although old, when she was left in a field at the head of so many workers, how well she made those labourers go! Here our Lord’s parable could very well be applied: that the last would have greater wages than the first (cf. Mt 20:16). She, old as she was, did more than a young woman, but a cold one with a sluggish spirit, of those who do not work out of love and eagerness to give this to the Beloved, and so seek to store up treasures for eternal life (cf. Mt 6:20). A soul that knows how to trade well with the talents Jesus gave her, even if she had only one, knows how to do so much that she multiplies them by hundreds. And many who have the fortune to have an abundance of them are not able to accumulate others, but with their indolence end by losing everything (cf. Mt 25:14–30). Oh! how many we see continually!”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 510–512; 236–237)

“… I saw that the Road where I was was full of thistles and very disastrous on every side, a mountain to cross and full of most cruel thorns. Nothing frightened me because at once I saw at the Top of this prepared for me things very great and beautiful beyond words; you will have everything when you have arrived up there. Oh! what magnificence of treasures! all the Suffering I had seen seemed nothing to me in comparison with the enjoyment prepared for me and for a time it remained so impressed on me that I always seemed to see my good, the union I felt, I can say I continually feel, is very great. Oh! my beloved, Consume me!” (from the Memoirs, 1.1, p. 105)

“my good gave me new graces by giving me instructions on the way of perfection. Oh! how I saw myself annihilated, and almost lost in my nothingness, a desire to destroy myself, and to be despised, it left me like one starving, the last of my Sisters seemed to me far more than I, as I always keep alive the conviction, my God! and how so much mercy to one so unworthy; Love that destroys me within this heart of yours which is swollen to such a point that I can no longer withstand it my bones! my good!” (from the Memoirs, 4.4, p. 14)

“nothing is able to make me feel agitation indeed in contradictions I feel a matchless calm and so in correcting I do not know however much I strive I cannot utter the words with the least zeal! what Grace, sweet love of mine! I feel there is in me One who does and says everything, he notes for me the smallest things. I see a calm over all my action and a perfect abandonment in his hands of everything that happens to me.

The taste for Holy Poverty is matchless: anxious to work for the glory of God and the Charity of the Neighbour I would do everything to relieve the poor sick and for the salvation of souls when someone says to me: you saved me, I was in the abyss and you saved me, Oh! what I feel my God, this is all my delight and my comfort in work in labours it is everything to me for my Dear and sweet Saviour” (from the Memoirs, 5.3, pp. 109–110)

“if I could describe what I feel on my part in this so sweet union, I could stay whole hours. The fire, the knowledge of certain spiritual things for other souls and for myself, the sensible taste for all that is of humility, the eagerness to be humbled and vivid desire to be despised by all, an inexpressible joy in being able to hide everything so that all may have nothing but compassion in bearing with me, so wretched as I am, and all this I feel with conviction I am, so wretched that I am ashamed of myself. What beautiful lessons I receive on how to busy myself in his Work, and in these raptures, in these days always warnings and teachings on how I must behave and act Oh! my Love, Sweetest Master, Wisest! I can truly say I am the true ass of Balaam or (ass of his Work who am so ignorant that I am not able to say a word well if he, my Saviour and master, did not teach me.”

(from the Memoirs, 5.4, pp. 5–7)

Annex 35 — Retreat 4

“…Oh! with what fire I feel myself burning! My God I can no more, I feel myself failing, Oh! when will be that day when you will open this prison to me and I shall fly away with you? Not to flee suffering, no!”.

(Mother Rosa, Memoirs, 1.1, p. 106)

“… I was ravished in Spirit and enjoyed a perfect union with my good. Oh! being of my living, I feel I am dying, your love makes me agonise. I saw many good souls who, out of too much fear, did not receive those graces that my good held prepared, but their fear led them to mistrust and so they stayed always doubtful and perplexed and for this could never come to take the sweet balm of the love of Jesus, Oh! Love! and do not fear the beloved, but fear only to displease him by falling. The sorrow is strong and inexpressible but the thought of mercy is matchless, a glance at the tabernacle is enough to see how much dear Love Jesus did for us Oh! Life of my Life!” (from the Memoirs, 1.1, pp. 54–55)

“… Remember, my Soul, the evening of 17 1875, Live in God alone and seek nothing else. Converse with him and seek no other relief than in him; in him let everything suffice you, an anguish that assailed me, I began to pray and a voice said to me thus, as is written above; Yes my good in you alone! and with him I stayed and he always comforted me and I asked about a person, and at once he revealed everything to me… I found in my Good true consolation, he assured me peace on many of my doubts, and I remained so tranquil in conscience that I enjoyed a heavenly peace and it still continues with me; I spent the night clasped to my good Oh! joy! I was dying so great was the love I felt, not a single instant did I have outside him, my Eternal my all who can describe what you do and communicate to the soul and what it experiences in you; Today in you and you for me live, I feel that I have no other life than yours, a calm, an inner peace I cannot describe, I speak, before me I feel and to put it better my Spirit feels there is something, that is felt and not seen with bodily eyes but the intellect sees and understands all.”

(from the Memoirs, 4.3, pp. 15 and 16)

Annex 36 — Retreat 5

“My voice commands me to run, and everyone persecutes me because I run too fast”

My voice:

— It is time to advance into the fields and sow with courage! — My God, your slave is ready!

So, running, at every moment I met people, and shepherds who troubled me, telling me that I ran too fast in sowing, that the harvest would not be at all good. At last to these were added also great shepherds, who grumbled a great deal. A sort of panic seized me and I almost slowed down the work.

My voice: — Oh! what are you doing?

Without heeding anything else I set about running still faster. Oh! what happened to me! A superior of the shepherds stops me, scolds me and with not very gentle insults says that I am proud and that I see nothing but the satisfaction of having fields to give vent to my pride, that I aim only at having estates and fields.

Oh! how I felt my chest tighten: as if between two very big stones I felt it being crushed. I went on saying to myself: how must I conduct myself? My voice does not err, and yet it is always the one that commands me to run; and everyone persecutes me because I run more than anything; to these are joined also my fellow workers, who grumble and complain because I make them work too much; not only that, but it pains them to see my continual walking without giving myself respite, that I rush on too much. They do not at all accept this way of mine. And several times they say to me:

— It is time to stop and arrange things so that you need not scourge yourself so much in this way.

My God! what to do? Is the voice that commands me to run not yours? Perhaps that ugly one is trying to deceive me?

How I had to struggle! My human nature joined with what they said: it took their side entirely and associated itself perfectly with them, and would gladly have put into practice what they said, that is, to stop. Thus besieged, I prayed to God to take me out of so painful a state. Was I mistaken? Weeping, I lay with my face on the ground. My voice:

— These people speak humanly. Go forward, follow me!

Oh my Love! your slave wants nothing but to carry out your orders perfectly!” (from Trials and Consolations, pp. 404–405)

Annex 37 — Retreat 6

“… In the year one thousand 869, 13 October, I made the holy exercises. From the first day my Eternal Father made me a gift, in my cell I stayed in contemplation while my Eternal One stretched out his right hand over me and gave me infinite graces. Oh! my Love! Teaching me to distinguish well the true spirit from the false; he gave me very great consolations Oh! my God! Oh! how happy those souls must be who have given themselves to the contemplative life; blessed in this Life and in Eternity. Wretched me who am always in the midst of the world Oh! my love, in three days I shall leave this cell of mine and again be in the midst of the affairs of your work; my Love, I must give justice to the Truth: although in the midst of so much tumult of an abyss of business yet I am never deprived of union with my God indeed for some time, since he furnished me with that dear treasure, I always See him at my sides and it is a cloud, something beautiful a being is seen that it contains because as I said above I already saw it, each time it becomes denser and rosy a voice comes forth that makes me feel in paradise and I remain absorbed, it tells me how I must conduct myself, when I do not know what to do and answer I consult it and it answers me, I stop and look at it and ask it: suggest, for I do not know what to say, my being, my dear Love! Because I am convinced that it is He who is within it, I hear the voice Oh! what it brings me I cannot say but it never reaches the point of rapture because his Word does not lie: no one will ever notice it Oh! sweet Love of mine! God, for it is he, because what he suggests to me all succeeds excellently, and Peace in the tribulations, which are matchless! Thus taught by my Eternal Father the Being of my living Jesus I obtain everything, it turns out perfect according to his Will. Oh! that your slave may never desire anything but to please you”.(from the Memoirs, 1.1., pp. 86–87)

“… Oh! what I felt! Oh! my Love, you alone could tell what these Visits of yours produced in me: strength still for Suffering, Resignation to your divine Will Oh! my Love! When I had finished reciting the office I thanked my good for so great a favour to a wretched sinner, a loathsome worm of the earth! but it is not I who live, my Jesus lives in me – not content I went to the Church to thank him (although it was far away and in such poor health as I had and I suffered much to go there. But my good consoled me just as much. They were about to give the Holy Blessing and the Blessed Sacrament was exposed. I saw the most precious Blood of my good, and what did it produce in me? Oh! my Love! you alone could tell it, who worked in me, I remained in ecstasy and could not and knew not how to say anything more and everything is little and nothing that can be said to a God so Merciful towards a poor ignorant creature. After a good while I turned to my Father St Francis and to all the Seraphim and cherubim that they might sing hymns of grace and thanksgiving for me to my God!” (from the Memoirs, 1.1., pp. 12–13)

… while I found myself closely united to my God, a most vivid light appeared to me, my cloud; but this time it opened and I saw most clearly my Eternal All who had stretched his right hand over my head, wholly intoxicated and very well assured of being guided by him. All the doubts that came to me last evening in the examination ceased, a thousand fears wanted to disturb me; but now I am most tranquil. Oh! my Master, how quickly you know how to dissolve every fear and give back to the soul peace, comfort, strength in a sea of worries and anguish where I find myself in this Work…” (from the Memoirs, 4.1., p. 18)

“… This morning my Beloved led me for a minute into his dwelling, let me taste his delicacies, but the enjoyment was very brief, so that I returned among the miseries of a painful life, as I find myself now. Only that today the fire devoured me…” (from the Memoirs, 3, p. 10)

Annex 38 — Retreat 7

What confusion was mine when I saw myself supported and raised up by my God! Oh! sweet Love of mine! But I could say nothing more. He made the sign of the cross on my forehead and said to me.

— Leave this wood, anoint your wounds, regain strength, for you must fight for my Work!

And he vanished. Full of strength I opened the little jar of ointment given to me by the gracious old woman and dressed the deepest wounds. And I resumed my journey, preparing myself for the struggle, which was not slow in coming.

They were armed men, whom I found after a long stretch of road. They were laying waste a strong and well-built edifice; I cried out with all the strength I had:

— Stop, in God’s name!

They, hearing such loud shouting, looked like so many drunkards; they looked at me and stood waiting for me. When I arrived (I said to them):

— Why do you intend to do so much harm? who are you? who sent you? Do you perhaps think this edifice has no one to defend it? Withdraw!

And still astonished they listened to me; they took up their tools and went away. One who was their leader left me with this word:

— I shall return furnished with powers!

My God, what will come of it? My voice: — Remove the rottenness that is inside!

At once I made a search and found one of those workers who had worked so cunningly that everything might be destroyed and, together with another, had arranged everything; I seized their plots, I intercepted their communications; and the one who said to me: I shall come with powers! was able to obtain nothing.

The edifice resumed its original foundation: the tumults disappeared and, running swiftly in every work of charity, it was a delight… Seeing that I did not give in at all to their threats, they resolved to seize me to reduce me to a bad state. But no! I stood firm, knowing that I was doing my duty as a slave, since my Lord so wished, I was not intimidated in the least; when one of these, in a rage, gives me so strong a slap; and I, so happy, turned round so that she might give me another. But in an instant they stop and, as if frightened, take to flight. Who could it be? Turning, I saw it was a tall young man, with a stern face; I stood for an instant looking at him, hesitant myself. He added:

— Do not be afraid! and he took off his cloak. Oh! my angel!” (from Trials and Consolations, pp. 283–285)

Annex 39 — Retreat 8

“My Crucified One! I was very deformed, and by his grace he made me beautiful, adorning me with his graces; he stripped me of the old self and I remained clothed as a gentle creature.

My Crucified One! He taught me to suffer and, like the honey of bees, shut up in those precious nests of wax, he kept suffering for me: it was changed into sweetness. Every now and then he gave me some of this juice to taste, and with sublime lessons made me understand how such exquisiteness is drawn from suffering, while nature rebelled against it.

My Crucified One subdues the human nature, gives vigour, energy and strength to the spirit which, victorious, lords it over all the faculties, and they are so well kept subject; self-love is dissipated and vanishes, is lost and even one’s own name is forgotten. Pride is conquered and looked upon as an instrument of disdain, as an enemy. One feels great pleasure when one sees them crushed and oppressed. Great consolation is felt by the will, which is overbearing, and this my Crucified One has exchanged for his own! It is sweet, infinitely pleasant no longer to possess it. Oh! how it would have rebelled if he had not nailed it!

My Crucified One! when, face down on the ground, having no more strength from the oppression of sorrow, I was choking, he raised me up and nourished me with his love. If my bones bent, my Crucified One filled me with the nectar of his love.

So, walking among crags and woods, always on the path marked by his footsteps, I did not notice that, all pricked, I was in pain, I felt a giant’s strength when I found myself face to face with people who said all sorts of rude things to me.

My Crucified One! he showed himself beautiful to me and took great delight in what I was suffering; then my love grew towards my persecutors and, if it had not been that they were offending God, I would have wished that they had been doubled. I found that they were leading me from Pilate and the judges; I was ashamed, but in my mind I meditated on the steps of my Saviour.

My Crucified One had pity on me and, enlightening me with his light, once more made me regain reason and intellect; full of knowledge I saw the abyss in which I found myself. Oh! divine Majesty, what a beautiful work! With strength and vigour I undertook the work of my journey; in a flash, I find the path.

My Crucified One gives me the sweetest bread of angels and gives me a cloud for a guide. Oh sweet journey! delightful the conversations by which, along it, I was held back! I ran so swiftly that no human creature could reach me; neither mountains nor rivers were able to halt my journey. The sweetnesses of the Beloved were continual and all the suffering was such that several times I fell in a faint.

My Crucified One showed me his wounds and I, full of shame, covered my face. I learned much, and I took refuge in those wounds; and my Crucified One was pleased with it.”

(from Trials and Consolations, pp. 49–50; 52–54)

“… Eternal Father, ah! communicate yourself to me in this communion of mine by giving me your divine Son, as you gave him for the redemption of the human race, so that he may redeem in me all my senses, leaving me wholly free from their slavery, and chained by your mercy, and that I may always remain a slave of your every will, as I already am a slave. And you, in telling me the essence of your love, grant that I may be filled with that alone. Hand me Jesus with your delicate hand. Yes, my only being of my living, you are the all, because when I possess you, I have everything in you… I have all.” (from Rosa Gattorno, a Mother, pp. 27–28)

“… My Good gave me so much sweetness in opening his side to me, and it seemed that into this heart of his that sweetest honey of his love was poured. Ah! how my part has swollen, my ribs. Ah! Love! why on so perverse a creature do you pour so many graces? Ah yes! I am infamous, but you are my master and do and undo in your servant what you please. I have no more tastes, I have no more pleasures: only you! and for you I live in order to die in you…”. (from the Memoirs, 4.5., p. 21ff.)
